Purpose

We want to know what cutoffs are likely appropriate to decide “good” (green), “be wary” (yellow) and “maybe don’t use” (red) for some of the measures in our datasets.

So to do this, we summarized all the values across datasets

So, based on Figure 3, we could just use the SD value we have, and say 4 * SD (80), you are in the red. Or we could argue an increment of 25 makes more sense, and do the 1, 2, and 3 * 25 cutoffs. Either way seems like it would be fine.

Median Correlations

Looking at Figure 5, I think we could evaluate the dataset as a whole, check the maximum observed, and if the maximum observed correlation falls below 0.5, that is something to flag.

Relative Standard Deviations

The overall distribution in Figure 7 looks like the better one to use, so we will take it, and find the median value, and the SD’s.

PC That Captures 90% of Cumulative Variance

In Figure 10, the log transformed PC-90 looks almost normal(ish). What would the cutoffs be if we used this log-distribution to calculate a mean and SD??

The only issue is, the mean, median and mode don’t capture the central location that the eye does. So I’m going with 0.5.

After looking at all of the above, Hunter was like, well what if we just look at the things that are above 0.8 or 1? That is what I did in Figure 13, using a median of 1, treating the distribution as one sided, and then adding the SD values to the 1. I think this makes much more sense.
